classification.difficultyReason: Match ten exponential graphs using direction, reflection, horizontal asymptote and y-intercept.

inlines.text: Match the equation to the graph.

spec.description: Decreasing positive exponential; intercept 1; both axes and curve have end arrows. Source teal curve mapped to house blue; ordinary axes black.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and intercept visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The graph decreases, has $y$-intercept $1$ and approaches $y=0$ from above, so $y=6^{-x}$.

spec.description: Decreasing curve below dashed asymptote 2, intercept 1, crossing the x-axis to the right; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and numerical labels visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The asymptote is $y=2$. The curve decreases below it and has $y$-intercept $-1+2=1$, so $y=-6^x+2$.

spec.description: Increasing positive exponential, intercept 1, approaching the x-axis to the left; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and intercept visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The graph increases, has $y$-intercept $1$ and approaches $y=0$ from above to the left, so $y=6^x$.

spec.description: Increasing negative exponential, intercept -1, approaching the x-axis from below to the right; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and intercept visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: Reflecting $y=6^{-x}$ across the $x$-axis gives an increasing curve below $y=0$ with intercept $-1$, so $y=-6^{-x}$.

spec.description: Decreasing negative exponential, intercept -1, approaching the x-axis from below to the left; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and intercept visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: Reflecting $y=6^x$ across the $x$-axis gives a decreasing curve below $y=0$ with intercept $-1$, so $y=-6^x$.

spec.description: Decreasing exponential, intercept -1, approaching dashed asymptote -2 from above to the right; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and numerical labels visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The decreasing curve is above its asymptote $y=-2$. Its $y$-intercept is $1-2=-1$, so $y=6^{-x}-2$.

spec.description: Increasing curve below dashed asymptote 2, intercept 1, crossing the x-axis to the left; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and numerical labels visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The increasing curve approaches $y=2$ from below to the right. Its $y$-intercept is $-1+2=1$, so $y=-6^{-x}+2$.

spec.description: Increasing negative exponential below dashed asymptote -2, intercept -3; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and numerical labels visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The increasing curve approaches $y=-2$ from below to the right. Its $y$-intercept is $-1-2=-3$, so $y=-6^{-x}-2$.

spec.description: Decreasing curve below dashed asymptote -2, intercept -3; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and numerical labels visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The decreasing curve approaches $y=-2$ from below to the left. Its $y$-intercept is $-1-2=-3$, so $y=-6^x-2$.

spec.description: Decreasing positive exponential above dashed asymptote 2, intercept 3; arrowed axes and curve.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and numerical labels visible; equation hidden.

answer.worked: The decreasing curve approaches $y=2$ from above to the right. Its $y$-intercept is $1+2=3$, so $y=6^{-x}+2$.
